rv.q: Rachel Kaly subverts the trauma comedy show by leaning into the strangest, most upsetting parts of her life and presenting them as everyday, embedded into the strangeness of life itself.
Either way, it’s worth celebrating a comedian who dares to speak what some might say should remain unspoken (the doctor in the audience did discharge her, in case you were wondering).
Rachel Kaly turns a lifetime of intake forms into a fearless, squirm-inducing hour of comedy that rewards anyone who shares her bedside manner and earns every uncomfortable laugh.

cn.t: Critics praise Kaly's disarmingly funny, darkly compelling solo show about mental health struggles, finding her deadpan delivery and unflinching honesty both laugh-out-loud hilarious and uncomfortably relatable across 70 minutes.

ta: 530 West 27th St, Sixth Floor, New York, NY
